url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

message.content:
Below is a **sample “Startup Stats” API** that you can use as a reference or even implement in your own service.  
It’s a REST‑style API (you could also expose it via GraphQL if you prefer).  
Feel free to tweak the endpoints, query parameters, or response shape to match your data source (Crunchbase, AngelList, PitchBook, your own database, etc.).

---

## 1. Base URL

```
https://api.yourstartupstats.com/v1
```

> *Replace `yourstartupstats.com` with your own domain or the provider’s domain.*

---

## 2. Authentication

All endpoints require an **API key** passed in the `Authorization` header:

```
Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_API_KEY>
```

> *If you’re using a third‑party provider (Crunchbase, AngelList, etc.), use their key format.*

---

## 3. Endpoints

| Method | Endpoint | Description | Query Params | Sample Response |
|--------|----------|-------------|--------------|-----------------|
| `GET` | `/startups` | List startups (paginated) | `page`, `per_page`, `search`, `location`, `industry`, `min_funding`, `max_funding` | See below |
| `GET` | `/startups/{id}` | Get a single startup by ID | None | See below |
| `GET` | `/startups/{id}/funding` | Funding history for a startup | `page`, `per_page` | See below |
| `GET` | `/startups/{id}/employees` | Employee count & distribution | `year` | See below |
| `GET` | `/metrics/industry` | Aggregate metrics by industry | `year` | See below |
| `GET` | `/metrics/location` | Aggregate metrics by location | `year` | See below |

> **Note:** All responses are JSON. Pagination uses `page` and `per_page` (default 20, max 100).

---

## 4. Sample Responses

### 4.1 List Startups

```
GET /startups?page=1&per_page=5&search=fintech&min_funding=500000
```

```json

  "page": 1,
  "per_page": 5,
  "total": 237,
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "startup_12345",
      "name": "FinTech Innovators",
      "website": "https://fintechinnovators.com",
      "location": "San Francisco, CA",
      "industry": "FinTech",
      "funding_total_usd": 1250000,
      "funding_rounds": 3,
      "employees": 42,
      "last_funding_date": "2024-02-15",
      "valuation_usd": 7500000,
      "description": "A platform that automates small‑business lending."
    },
    ...
  ]
}
```

### 4.2 Single Startup

```
GET /startups/startup_12345
```

```json
{
  "id": "startup_12345",
  "name": "FinTech Innovators",
  "website": "https://fintechinnovators.com",
  "location": "San Francisco, CA",
  "industry": "FinTech",

  "funding_rounds": 3,
  "employees": 42,

  "valuation_usd": 7500000,
  "description": "A platform that automates small‑business lending.",
  "founders": [
    {"name": "Alice Smith", "role": "CEO"},
    {"name": "Bob Johnson", "role": "CTO"}
  ],
  "social_links": {
    "twitter": "https://twitter.com/fintechinnov",
    "linkedin": "https://linkedin.com/company/fintechinnov"
  }
}
```

### 4.3 Funding History

```
GET /startups/startup_12345/funding?page=1&per_page=10
```

```json

  "page": 1,
  "per_page": 10,
  "total": 3,
  "data": [
    {
      "round": "Series B",
      "amount_usd": 800000,
      "date": "2024-02-15",
      "investors": ["Venture Capital Firm A", "Angel Investor X"]
    },
    {
      "round": "Series A",
      "amount_usd": 300000,
      "date": "2023-07-01",
      "investors": ["Venture Capital Firm B"]
    },
    {
      "round": "Seed",
      "amount_usd": 200000,
      "date": "2022-03-12",
      "investors": ["Angel Investor Y"]
    }
  ]
}
```

### 4.4 Employees

```
GET /startups/startup_12345/employees?year=2024
```

```json

  "startup_id": "startup_12345",
  "year": 2024,
  "total_employees": 42,
  "distribution": {
    "Engineering": 18,
    "Product": 8,

```

  "year": 2024,

    {
      "name": "FinTech",

### 4.6 Location Metrics

```
GET /metrics/location?year=2024
```

```json

  "year": 2024,
  "locations": [
    {
      "city": "San Francisco",
      "state": "CA",
      "startups_count": 300,
      "total_funding_usd": 900000000,
      "average_valuation_usd": 9500000
    },
    {
      "city": "New York",
      "state": "NY",
      "startups_count": 250,
      "total_funding_usd": 750000000,
      "average_valuation_usd": 8800000
    }
  ]
}
```

---

## 5. Example Code Snippets

### 5.1 Python (requests)

```python
import requests

BASE = "https://api.yourstartupstats.com/v1"
API_KEY = "YOUR_API_KEY"

headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {API_KEY}"}

# Get a list of fintech startups that raised >$500k
resp = requests.get(
    f"{BASE}/startups",
    headers=headers,
    params={"search": "fintech", "min_funding": 500000, "page": 1, "per_page": 10}
)
print(resp.json())
```

### 5.2 JavaScript (fetch)

```js
const BASE = "https://api.yourstartupstats.com/v1";
const API_KEY = "YOUR_API_KEY";

fetch(`${BASE}/startups?search=fintech&min_funding=500000&page=1`, {
  headers: {
    Authorization: `Bearer ${API_KEY}`
  }
})
  .then(r => r.json())
  .then(data => console.log(data))
  .catch(err => console.error(err));
```

---

## 6. Using Third‑Party Providers

If you don’t want to build your own data layer, you can tap into existing APIs:

| Provider | API | Key Features | Notes |
|----------|-----|--------------|-------|
| Crunchbase | `https://api.crunchbase.com/v3.1/` | Company profiles, funding rounds, employee data, market trends | Requires paid plan for full access |
| AngelList | `https://api.angel.co/1/` | Startup listings, funding, team, location | Free tier limited to 1000 requests/day |
| PitchBook | `https://api.pitchbook.com/` | Detailed financials, valuations, M&A activity | Enterprise‑grade, expensive |
| CB Insights | `https://api.cbinsights.com/` | Market intelligence, funding, exits | Paid API |

> **Tip:** Most of these services return data in JSON; you can map their fields to the schema above.

---

## 7. Error Handling

All error responses follow this structure:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": 400,
    "message": "Invalid API key",
    "details": "The provided API key is missing or expired."
  }
}
```

| HTTP Code | Meaning |
|-----------|---------|
| 400 | Bad request (missing/invalid params) |
| 401 | Unauthorized (invalid API key) |
| 403 | Forbidden (rate limit exceeded) |
| 404 | Not found (e.g., startup ID does not exist) |
| 429 | Too many requests (rate limit) |
| 500 | Internal server error |

---

## 8. Rate Limits

| Plan | Requests per minute | Requests per day |
|------|---------------------|------------------|
| Free | 60 | 1,000 |
| Basic | 300 | 10,000 |
| Pro | 1,200 | 50,000 |
| Enterprise | Custom | Custom |

> *Adjust these numbers to fit your usage patterns.*

---

## 9. Next Steps

1. **Choose a data source** (Crunchbase, AngelList, your own database).  
2. **Set up authentication** (API key, OAuth, etc.).  
3. **Implement the endpoints** (REST or GraphQL).  
4. **Add caching** (Redis, in‑memory) to reduce external API calls.  
5. **Document the API** (OpenAPI/Swagger) so developers can consume it easily.  

Feel free to copy the endpoint definitions above into an OpenAPI spec or Swagger UI to generate interactive docs.

---

### Quick Test

If you want to see a quick demo, you can use the following mock endpoint (replace `<YOUR_API_KEY>` with any string):

```
https://mockapi.io/projects/64c3f5b2e3a1b2c3d4e5f6/startups
```

> *MockAPI.io lets you create a fake REST API quickly. Just paste the URL into your browser or use `curl`.*

---

Let me know if you’d like a deeper dive into any specific part (e.g., pagination logic, GraphQL schema, or how to integrate Crunchbase data). Happy building!
